# Design doc for QTD1

This design doc is used to align on a high-level plan for the reimplementation of the QTD1 app functionality.

## Background

-   QTD1 was developed first, based on request by internal management.
-   Its methodology is very similar to the section on "Quantitative decision criteria and trial performance metrics" in the Lalonde et al (2007) paper.
    -   The names are different from those in the paper.
-   `QTD1_demo.pptx` shows a presentation on how the app would be used.
-   The computation code of QTD1 is organized in an R package format, but was never released externally.
-   The GUI code is in Java and was developed by a contractor and is not available.
    -   Shiny was not yet available at the time of development, therefore Java was used.
    -   That should not be a problem because the app consists of a single page with a few input fields only and a single plot output, so we can implement it without having the Java code.
-   To start the binary application, unzip file `QTD_1.1.1.zip` and execute `bin/QTD.exe`
    -   Note: First need to install old Java SDK and JRE for 32bit on Windows, see [here](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/javase-jdk8-downloads.html).

## Motivation

-   The current QTD1 app is not working correctly anymore (reproducibility issues).
-   The IT security department does not like the fact that the app is installed on desktop computers directly, instead of being hosted on a server.

Therefore a new implementation is needed.

## Objectives

Develop a Shiny app that replicates the functionality of QTD1:

-   R code should be available when requested by the user.
-   The underlying computations shall be implemented in an open source R package, that can also be used without the Shiny app.
    -   The names of quantities etc should be based on the LaLonde paper instead of on the QTD1 app, to be easily useable by external users too.
-   Follow good software engineering practices, in particular the [`openstatsguide`](https://openstatsware.org/guide.html).

## Proposal

-   Develop the required statistical calculations in new functions in the `rpact` R package
    -   It fits within the scope of the package because `rpact` includes fixed design analyses and operating characteristics
    -   In terms of additional statistical methods, little will be needed (maybe score test based confidence intervals for binary proportions)
    -   Detailed design to be included here below later
    -   The code will be automatically included in the validation process of the `rpact` package
    -   Open source available on CRAN as part of `rpact`
-   Develop the Shiny app to be a module of the RPACT Cloud
    -   Code would not be public, but free usage up to certain usage limit for the public
    -   The app would be hosted on the RPACT Cloud, see [here](https://cloud.rpact.com)
    -   Installation as part of RPACT Cloud in Novartis internally, easily available in the existing RPACT Cloud deployment, deployment instructions and source code available in the Novartis-specific GitHub repository, see [here](https://github.com/rpact-com/rpact.cloud.novartis)
    -   Other companies licensing RPACT Cloud can also use the app then internally in their own RPACT Cloud
